$comment: Behavioural conformance for the pure decision logic, executed by BOTH runtimes, and
the good/bad references every gate must prove before a run starts.
Why this file exists: tests/test_parity.py proves a marker STRING exists in each
build. That catches a feature nobody ported; it cannot catch a feature ported
WRONGLY, and it once passed a row whose JS marker was a comment describing the
mechanism. Every drift this repo has recorded was in logic of exactly this shape: a
pure function over plain data. So both runtimes are asked the same questions here and
must return the same answers.
`instruments` says what each function IS. A `gate` accepts or rejects, so it carries
both a `good` reference it must accept and a `bad` one it must catch, and the
structural rule below is enforced on it. A `transform` maps input to output with no
verdict, so good/bad does not apply and only the answers are checked.
THE STRUCTURAL RULE: every gate must have at least one `good` case and at least one
`bad` case, and in each runtime the bad references must produce at least one answer
no good reference produces. A gate whose bad references all answer the same as its
good ones has not been shown to reject anything, and a check that cannot fail is
indistinguishable from no check. This is the rule the parity markers failed for
years, and the rule catchRate failed by counting a partial as a catch.
It runs at preflight, before any API call, not only in CI: a deployed copy with a
broken gate refuses to start rather than producing a report nobody can check.
A case may carry `out_by_runtime` instead of `out` when the two builds legitimately
answer differently because the PLATFORM differs - URL parsing is the real instance.
That is not an escape hatch for drift: it pins both answers, so either one moving is
a failure, and `why` must say what makes the difference correct.
`python_cases` holds gates the JS build genuinely does not have, each with the reason,
the same way tests/test_parity.py keeps PYTHON_ONLY honest.

Content-token overlap is 1.000 because 'not' is a stopword and 'do' is two characters, so every threshold passes it and the opposite claim was stamped preRegistered: true with the certainty label. Third time a similarity measure here has been blind to a negation: the character bag scored 'output is stable' against 'output is unstable' at 1.000, SequenceMatcher 0.941, and the token measure that replaced both scores this at 1.000. in: H1: Under matched calorie deficits, IF and CCR produce statistically similar fat loss; the difference is adherence rather than metabolic superiority
No meaningful difference: under matched calorie deficits, IF and CCR produce statistically similar fat loss, and the difference is adherence, not metabolic superiority
hyp_mismatch.why: NOT a reference, deliberately untagged. A NAMED LIMIT, and this case's fifth reversal is its last: v1.10.1 protected it, v1.11.0 killed it, and the direction-aware fix cannot save it either - because it is genuinely inseparable from the attack. This rewording swaps 'not metabolic superiority' for the synonymous 'rather than metabolic superiority', scoring 0.855 on character similarity - INSIDE the surgical-deletion band (0.821-0.977) that must fire: a verdict that deletes 'no' and keeps everything else is the mirror attack at 0.928-0.977, and no lexical bar separates a synonymous contrastive from a surgical deletion. Moving the bar above 0.855 would re-open the mirror for short hypotheses, whose token overlap is a perfect 1.000 in the coverage check below - the exact v1.11 bug. What it costs, corrected after measurement: the STAMP. v1.11 gated BOTH the number and text paths with the same symmetric check - its own docstring claimed this shape kept its stamp via the text path, which was false in its shipped code - so this verdict is marked post-hoc in both. That is the understating direction the repo's policy explicitly chooses, and it is stated as the stamp, not softened to a label. Expected True records what the code does and why nothing better is available; the compact-rewording case beside this one is the good reference that proves the fix works where separation exists

in: IF and CCR produce statistically similar fat loss under matched calorie deficits
No meaningful difference: under matched calorie deficits, IF and CCR produce statistically similar fat loss, and the difference is adherence, not metabolic superiority
hyp_mismatch.why: The GOOD reference for the direction-aware rule: a COMPACT rewording of a registered null drops the negation-bearing framing along with real content (character similarity 0.479-0.697), which is what separates it from a surgical deletion (0.821-0.977). The ADD direction still fires categorically, and the DROP direction fires on near-identity - so this faithful rewording keeps its number-path stamp while the pinned surgical deletions stay killed. The v1.10.1 false accusation is closed without re-opening the v1.11.0 mirror, on the only axis where the two families separate at all
